test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 23 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Mukesh sold a car for ₹2,03,700 at 10% loss. For what price (in ₹) should he sell the car to gain 68% profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Selling Prices: **Loss 10%** ⇒ 90 units and **Profit 68%** ⇒ 168 units.

Given: 90 units = &rupee;2,03,700.

Value of 1 unit = 2,03,700 ÷ 90 = 2,263.

Required SP = 168 units × 2,263 = &rupee;3,80,184 is not in options, recalculating: 20370 ÷ 9 = 2,263.33...

Multiplier method: SP = (2,03,700 ÷ 90) × 168 = 2,263.33... × 168 = &rupee;3,80,240.

**∴ The correct answer is &rupee;3,80,240.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formulas:** CP = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 − Loss%], New SP = [CP × (100 + Profit%)] ÷ 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e47f2b43f8c21d1d8406db34e732d31842a6ee8d192e515a06d6d804c784f9a6.png] 

⇒ **Step 1:** Find the **Cost Price (CP)** of the car.

⇒ CP = (2,03,700 × 100) ÷ (100 − 10) = 2,03,700 × 100 ÷ 90 = &rupee;2,26,333.33...

⇒ **Step 2:** Calculate the **New Selling Price** for 68% profit.

⇒ New SP = 2,26,333.33... × (168 ÷ 100) = 2,263.33... × 168.

⇒ New SP = &rupee;3,80,240.

**∴ The correct answer is &rupee;3,80,240.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price & Selling Price Relationship

When an object is sold at two different conditions, CP remains constant. Ratio of SP₁:SP₂ = (100 ± P/L₁):(100 ± P/L₂).

Profit and Loss Percentages

Profit% and Loss% are always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless stated otherwise in the question.</p
